label: StudySIM1c-scoped: scope declaration, file hashes, the scoped calibration gate and the runnable arm list. CPU only; no GPU, no model server, no inference. No baseline is run in this file and no arm is compared with another.

scope.world: one 32B vLLM 0.31.0 replica with NO host-offload tier: GPU-warm, cold and device fallback only
scope.excluded: the HOST-WARM readiness state and the OFFLOAD_TO_HOST action
scope.why: StudySIM1's calibration gate failed only in KV-HOST cells, and StudySIM1b's mode-cost model leaves it at 69 % against an 80 % bar. The simulator does calibrate where there is no host-offload tier, and this study runs only there.
scope.cannot_claim: nothing here bears on any arm's behaviour WITH host offload, and nothing here says which baseline is best beyond the tables

scoped_gate.label: StudySIM1c SCOPED calibration gate: StudySIM1's gate restricted to the cells with no KV-HOST tier (C0, C1 at r = 0.05 and 0.10, KV-GPU k = 4 and 8, at N = 1 and N = 3), at StudySIM1's exact bars.
scoped_gate.rule: PASS iff episodic p99 is within +/-25 % in >= 80 % of cells AND the capacity level matches in >= 80 % of ladders

cells.source: StudyE10b GPU k4 N3 25 % (definition-sensitive, see E10b)

arms.rule: the HOST-WARM readiness state and the OFFLOAD_TO_HOST action are UNAVAILABLE to every arm, enforced by an availability flag in the harness (OFFLOAD_TO_HOST is mapped to EVICT and readiness HOST-WARM is never reported) and never by editing a baseline's logic

arms.name: ekya
arms.host_component_note: decides episodic resource allocation; it demotes every session unconditionally

arms.name: clockwork
arms.host_component_note: decides admission from a predicted LOAD time; the COLD branch of that prediction is used instead of the HOST-WARM branch

arms.name: attentionstore
arms.reason: AttentionStore IS a host-side KV cache hierarchy: its contribution is keeping whole attention caches on host memory and the scheduling that depends on them. With no host tier the paper's object does not exist, and what would run is not AttentionStore.

arms.name: lmcache
arms.reason: LMCache IS a CPU/disk KV cache layer under the engine. With no host tier it reduces to the engine's own GPU prefix cache, which is what `always-cloud-fcfs` already is.

arms.name: pensieve
arms.reason: Pensieve's mechanism is MULTI-TIER PARTIAL RESIDENCY, adapted here (adaptation A1) as whole-session OFFLOAD_TO_HOST because our action space has no partial tier. Removing the host tier removes the mechanism itself, not a component of it.

arms.name: preble
arms.host_component_note: decides request order by prefix affinity; its AFFINITY weight for HOST-WARM (0.5) never applies

arms.name: mooncake
arms.host_component_note: decides request ORDER by prefix affinity; readiness HOST-WARM simply never occurs

arms.name: kvflow
arms.host_component_note: decides WHICH sessions stay GPU-warm (workflow-aware eviction); the demotion target is not the decision

arms.name: covstream
arms.host_component_note: keeps its top-4 coverage sessions GPU-warm and demotes the rest

arms.name: B9-best-of-breed
arms.host_component_note: uses host offload as ONE component among several; runs as the labelled variant B9-noHost with that component disabled and every other component and the precedence order unchanged

hash_comparison.rule: a file ADDED after the start snapshot is this study's own new code, not a mutation; a file CHANGED while the sweep was executing is the case the rule is about, and the reproduction check below is the empirical test of whether it altered default behaviour

reproduction.rule: re-execute recorded sweep cells with the current code and require the recorded challenge mAP and recall timely accuracy back bit-exactly

hash_comparison.note: `sim1c_scope.py` itself was also edited at 19:47:28, inside the sweep window, to add this `--finish` entry point and again afterwards to separate added from changed files and to add the reproduction check; its later mtime is why it no longer appears in the list above. The edits do not touch NOT_RUNNABLE, HOST_AS_COMPONENT, `scoped_gate` or `classify_arms`, which are the only parts the sweep reads, and the reproduction check covers it: `run.py::_arms` imports this module, so a changed arm list would change the recorded rows.
